user: What are the sheltered rooms designated for use?
assistant: A safe room is a designated space for shelter during a tornado, ideally located below ground. However, during an event involving weapons of mass destruction, staying at home and sheltering in place might make an above-ground safe room a better option. This is because contaminants could potentially seep into rooms below ground level. An above-ground safe room should have no windows for optimal safety. Additionally, a bathroom can serve as a good shelter-in-place option, provided that it has no windows and all openings to the outside can be sealed.
user: What about public shelters?
assistant: Mass care sheltering involves living with many people in close quarters, which can be challenging. To prevent conflicts, cooperate with shelter managers and staff. Remember, alcohol and weapons are not allowed, and smoking is restricted.
Your stay may be brief, like during a tornado, or longer, like during a winter storm. Stay in the shelter until authorities say it’s safe to leave. Take turns listening to the radio and maintaining a 24-hour safety watch.
user: What are the recommendations for ensuring readiness?
assistant: Emergency preparedness simplifies decision-making and helps reduce fear, stress, and anxiety during a natural disaster. Make an emergency plan. Build or restock your emergency preparedness kit. Familiarize yourself with local emergency plans. Turn on your TV/radio. You’ll get the latest weather updates and emergency instructions. Know where to go. If you are ordered to evacuate, know the route and plan where you will go—check in with your friends and family. Keep your car fueled, in good condition, and stocked with emergency supplies and a change of clothes. Family Program Readiness Centers Family Readiness Centers are available to provide assistance and resources when needed. Your emergency planning should address the care of pets, aiding family members with access and functional needs, and safely shutting off utilities. To help you make a plan, visit  Ready.gov.
[The End of Previous Conversation]

View/Download the Disaster Preparedness Guide (PDF)
This page outlines what you need to be self-sufficient for at least seven days. The Emergency Preparation Checklist (PDF) provides a helpful general guideline for preparations to take before the next disaster strikes. 
The Family Disaster Plan (PDF) serves as a guide for your family both before and after a disaster occurs. Be sure to check out the list of items that should be included in your Family Disaster Kit (PDF.
Additionally, the Food and Water List (PDF) offers guidance on how to store, use, and maintain food and water during an emergency. You will also find information about resource establishments where you can purchase the necessary items for your emergency kit.
Don’t forget to include supplies for your pets.
